summary: env tag stripped during cross-account impersonation -> WIF->AssumeRole mapping fails for staging sandboxes
description:
Issue summary:
During JIT debugging access for staging sandboxes, the GCP->AWS token exchange (WIF -> AssumeRole) intermittently fails when the 'env' session tag is missing or empty after translation. This prevents internal SREs and CI runners from assuming scoped debug roles.

Impact:
- Several on-call sessions for staging and preprod environments failed to assume debug roles (denied by IAM) between 2026-03-01T09:10Z and 2026-03-01T12:40Z.
- Affects internal troubleshooting and block some dedicated/private onboarding runs which rely on the same token bridge.
- Not customer-facing (internal-support) but blocking deployment/customer-facing work for a subset of Dedicated onboarding.

Environment:
- Private deploy control plane + token-exchange service (token-bridge) in us-east region.
- Affected flows: GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) -> Redwood token-bridge -> AWS AssumeRole with session tags.

Steps to reproduce (observed / manual):
1) Use a GCP service account mapped to internal-debug@redwood (WIF flow).
2) Request a token via token-bridge that should include session tags: {project: "sandbox-x", env: "staging", requestor: "svc-internal"}.
3) Bridge performs exchange and calls AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with the mapped tags.
4) Observe AssumeRole denied if 'env' tag is absent/empty. Repeat multiple times: ~30% of attempts show missing 'env' on AWS side.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- token-bridge logs (2026-03-01T09:13:02Z): "trace=tb-8f3a: mapped_tags={project:sandbox-x, requestor:svc-internal} - missing env tag after normalize()"
- AWS STS response (2026-03-01T09:13:02Z): "AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sandbox-debug-role because session tag 'env' not allowed by policy"
- GCP audit entry (2026-03-01T09:12:58Z) shows an upstream attribute 'x-goog-env' present in token but later lost by token-bridge. Trace IDs: tb-8f3a, tb-8f9c.

Observed frequency: ~30% of token exchanges in the time window. Pattern appears correlated with concurrent bridge restarts or reconfig reloads.

Immediate business impact: Internal debug workflows fail, delaying Dedicated onboarding and incident response.

Workarounds tried:
- Manual assume-role using a privileged admin account (works) — not ideal.
- Re-deploy token-bridge to a previous version (temporarily reduces frequency)
- Short-term ACL added to role trust policy to allow fallback when env tag missing (Mitigation applied 2026-03-02 02:20Z)
comments: 2026-03-01 10:05 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer-facing impact: none. Notified infra oncall. Requested trace logs and sample request headers.

2026-03-01 11:15 - Infra Oncall (Diego Morales): Collected token-bridge traces (tb-8f3a, tb-8f9c). Noticing normalize() path sometimes drops 'env' when header key contains uppercase or unknown prefix.

2026-03-01 15:42 - Auth Engineer (Maya Singh): Confirmed WIF token includes 'x-goog-env' in 100% of incoming tokens. Bridge normalization rules filter unknown keys during hot-reload; race condition suspected.

2026-03-02 02:25 - Security (Jonah Lee): Temporary trust-policy fallback added to sandbox-debug-role to accept assume-role when env tag absent for principals with admin:debug override. This reduces operational impact but is temporary.

2026-03-04 09:10 - Token-bridge Owner (Priya Kapoor): Deployed candidate fix: ensure normalization retains recognized lowercase env key even during config reload. Running canary across 2 pods in us-east. Monitoring for 24h.

2026-03-05 14:00 - Diego Morales: Canary looks healthy; missing-tag error rate dropped from ~30% to <1% in canary. Preparing cluster-wide rollout and a follow-up test plan to validate under scale. Pending final PR review (see related PRs).
investigation_notes:
Timeline and hypotheses: initial traces show token contains env attribute, token-bridge normalize() path removes keys that don't match the current allowed-keys set. When the bridge reloads allowed-keys from SSM/ConfigStore concurrently with processing requests, there is a window where allowed-keys is temporarily an empty set -> env dropped. Repro reproduces under induced restarts. Confirmed by inserting additional logs in normalize() that show empty allowed-keys during restart. Root cause likely: non-atomic config reload + hot path using shared mutable set without lock.

Next steps already identified:
- Short-term: keep trust-policy fallback for sandbox debug roles (security-approved timeboxed exception).
- Medium-term: patch token-bridge to atomically swap allowed-keys and add unit+stress tests (PR #78).
- Long-term: add canary strategy for config reloads and add a guard to fail-safe to preserve known keys during empty config windows.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary role trust-policy fallback created 2026-03-02 (Security-approved) which restores operations. Patch submitted to token-bridge to perform atomic allowed-keys swap and to normalize keys case-insensitively (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/token-bridge/pull/78). Canary deployed 2026-03-04 and reduced missing-tag rate to <1%. Full rollout scheduled pending PR merge and additional load testing. Follow-up action: remove trust-policy fallback after rollout and create a runbook entry for emergency config reloads.
sre_action_items: deploy token-bridge patch to all us-east pods after PR approval
schedule rollback window and monitor token-bridge metrics (token_missing_env_count)
add runbook step: if token-bridge restart observed, check allowed-keys length before enabling traffic
